This is a many-to-one relationship from the perspective of the 2023 source being reused for different 2024 granular components, which is permitted.

comparisons.peer_summary: Net income for Consumer Lending increased $334 million to $3.2 billion, driven primarily by higher revenue including a $717 million increase in net interest income and an $85 million increase in noninterest income.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC describe revenue increases in their respective wealth and consumer lending divisions driven by components of net interest income and non-interest income. C reports a 2% increase in net interest income due to higher deposit spreads and volumes. BAC reports a $717 million increase in net interest income for Consumer Lending driven by higher loan balances, alongside an $85 million increase in noninterest income (primarily card income). While C focuses on investment fees for non-interest growth and BAC on card income, both segments show parallel strength in both NII and non-interest revenue streams contributing to overall segment growth.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management Net Interest Revenue Performance and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Wealth Management net interest revenues decreased 10% year-over-year to $7,313 million in 2024, primarily driven by lower average sweep deposits, partially offset by higher investment portfolio yields and lending growth.
comparisons.comparison: While both disclosures focus on Wealth Management net interest revenues, the trends diverge. C reports a 2% increase in Wealth segment net interest income driven by higher spreads and volumes. In contrast, MS reports a 10% decrease in Wealth Management net interest revenues to $7.3 billion, primarily driven by lower average sweep deposits. MS does cite partial offsetting factors like higher investment portfolio yields, similar to C's mention of higher yields/spreads, but the net outcome and primary driver (deposits/spreads vs. sweep deposit decline) are distinct.
